title: South End Community Centre construction approved
subtitle: Short-term rental licensing rules, other consent items and a Ward 5 town hall announcement.
overview: Council approved construction of the South End Community Centre at a project cost of $115.5 million, including $35.5 million in additional budget. The extra money comes mostly from the Parks and Recreation Development Charge Reserve Fund, with a smaller part from tax-supported debt. The item passed as part of the consent agenda. One councillor called it a historic step and said they hope for a groundbreaking this fall.

Council also directed staff to create a new schedule under the Business Licensing By-law to regulate short-term rental accommodations {{vote:m4}}. For residents, this means hosts will need a licence, and the rules are meant to protect long-term rental housing. A delegate supported the staff recommendation and pointed to the local housing shortage.

The consent agenda also covered other staff reports, including the property tax policy, revenue budgeting policy and internal audit work plan. Council passed a set of by-laws and adjourned. Two Ward 5 councillors announced a hybrid town hall on April 5 at 5 pm at Kortright Presbyterian Church, 55 Devere Drive. It will cover the tree protection by-law.

decisions.detail: Council approved construction at a project cost of $115.5 million, with $35.5 million in additional budget funded from the Parks and Recreation Development Charge Reserve Fund and tax-supported debt.
Council directed staff to create a new schedule under the Business Licensing By-law to license short-term rental accommodations, following the report's recommendations {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: Committee of the Whole consent agenda
decisions.detail: Council adopted the consent agenda, which bundled several staff reports, including the South End Community Centre funding and items such as the property tax policy and internal audit work plan.

debate: A delegate supported the staff recommendation, linking short-term rental rules to the local housing shortage and high rents. The delegate described rentals as a business model that turns homes into commercial assets.

The delegate said comparable Ontario municipalities limit the number of short-term rentals per licence and require the licensed property to be the host's primary residence. The delegate questioned why anyone would want more than one additional property per licensee.

A councillor asked how the rules would be enforced. Staff said enforcement would be both complaint-based and proactive. The company that first counted local listings would supply updated lists, and staff would compare them with licence records and follow up with education and enforcement.

A councillor raised a concern that some landlords use 30-day short-term rentals to avoid landlord-tenant rules. Staff said they had heard this during engagement. They said abuse is always possible, but the rules are meant to deter it.

Councillor Allt raised a point of privilege so that views of a councillor who was absent would be balanced. The mayor ruled it was not a point of privilege and said delegates and councillors may each state different views.
